cohort: Super-obese pregnant women (BMI >50 kg/m2 or weight >140 kg) who gave birth between January 1 and October 31, 2010 in Australia, compared to a cohort of non-super-obese pregnant women
finding: Super-obesity in pregnancy in Australia is associated with increased rates of pregnancy and birth complications, and with social disadvantage.
mod_finding: Super-obese women in Australia had a significantly higher risk of birth by cesarean section compared to other women.
birth_weight: Babies born to super-obese women had significantly higher rates of birthweight ≥ 4500 g
